$comment: The enforced gate on ambiguous watermarks (SPEC.md §7, issues #16 and #71).
tvtracker recorded most watches per episode, but a few titles carry watches only as
shows.watched_through — an absolute ordinal across the whole show, with no record of
which episodes it counted. Where that ordinal claims more watches than the episode rows
account for, and the show was not watched right through, the export simply does not say
which episodes those were. The conversion halts and names them rather than guess.
`credit` is an explicit list of episodes, never a count — a count would put the guess
back in the script. An EMPTY `credit` is a real answer: it records that the watermark is
stale and that nothing extra should be written for that show. The show keeps whatever
tvtracker is re-exported at cutover, so this file is not a checklist ticked once. A fresh
export with different stragglers halts on them, and an answer left here for a show that
no longer needs one halts too, rather than being inherited unread.

confirmations.title: Hudson & Rex
confirmations.reason: Adham's call, 2026-08-18: drop the watermark. It claims 60 of 122 episodes while the episode rows name 53, and those rows have real gaps — S1E1-10 and S2E8-11 — that a watermark of 60 contradicts. The 53 recorded watches stand; the 7 the watermark implies are not written, because nothing records which they were.

confirmations.title: Person of Interest
confirmations.reason: Adham's call, 2026-08-18: drop the watermark. It claims 7 of 103 episodes with no episode rows at all, so there is no evidence in either direction. The title stays in the library as a watchlist entry rather than carrying 7 watches nothing can place.
